## Audit items not yet fixed

Suspects from FABLE-AUDIT.md that nothing on main fixes. Each is verified at the cited line first; a confirmed defect gets a lock-in test and a negative control.

### Windows iocp and rio re-flush

Audit 88 and 124: measure on captain, then add re-flush counters if the measurement supports it.

From: Audit items 88, 124

### Generate LOAD.md's byte tables

The page's exact byte figures go stale with every merge. Generate them, with a CI check that the page matches the generator.

From: #721 follow-on

### Read the three thread rule counters on the production library

MAIN_THREAD_CALL_OVERLAP, CLIENT_SEND_TWO_THREADS and SEND_RESERVE_REFUSED_TAILS_HELD are counted in every build, and each is read by value in a test, but every such test links the development library (bin/test_wide_fill, tests/test_unit_server_send_reserve.cpp). Add a case to the production functional binary that breaks each of the two thread rules through the public API and reads the counters; the same case can check the API misuse count of a message left open at update, which no test reads.

From: Piece G, cold reader (counters and tests sections)

### Start order of one client's packets when its sending thread changes between flushes

On a transport that buffers payloads in the server's ring, a thread's unused chunk slots stay on its line until the flush. If one thread sends to a client, a checked main thread call that is not send_packets follows, and another thread then sends to the same client, the second thread's packets may sit in lower slots and leave first. rocketnet.h states it. Returning every line's chunk at each checked main thread call would keep start order; it costs a walk of the 64 lines a call.

From: Piece G, cold reader finding 2 (second case)

### Do not sleep after a partial sendmsg_x

A partial sendmsg_x result ends the call kept (sdk/rocketnet_msgx_send_runs.h), so the transmit worker marks the socket full and waits 1 ms (sdk/rocketnet_server_msgx_apple.cpp) although the socket took data. Loop again at once when the kept call made progress, and wait only when a call took nothing. Measured nowhere yet: the four space rows pass as it is.

From: Piece P cold read

### Hard-killed client cases: take the wire mark after the clients read the last pass's sends

posix_hk_quiesce (tests/functional/posix_hard_killed_client.cpp) updates the clients, then the server, then sends the server's packets, so a datagram the server sends in the last pass is counted sent at posix_hk_wire_mark and received after it. That datagram hides one real loss in lost_down, and a payload lost on the way then fails posix_hk_require_accounted with lost 0. Seen once on a parallel macOS run (send_to_closed_port, server portable, ipv6, client msgx: down 79/80, lost 0). Fix: end the quiesce with a client-only read pass before the mark, or mark the client and server reads at the same point.

From: Piece P CI read

### rio destroy: free the stopped lanes when one lane is stuck

rocketnet_server_rio_destroy returns before destroying any lane when one lane never reports stopped (a completion queue reported corrupt, or a send the kernel never completes). The lanes that did stop stay allocated until process exit. Measured as intended for this piece: the leak is bounded and named. Fix: destroy every lane that reports stopped and leak only the stuck one, as the create rollback already does (rocketnet_server_rio_create_leaks), with a unit case that holds one lane's sends.

From: Piece N (rio rebuilt), cold read

### Layout model coverage of the gso send step's order, held slot and plain resend

proofs/tla/RNGsoQueueBankLayout.tla models the claim, the id and the slot rule. lane->order (the gather's positions), send_step's held_slot and the position it resumes from, and resend_plain's first_slot arithmetic index the banks too and have no layout model or trace layer; they are covered by unit cases only.

From: Piece K, cold reader

### Packet id 0 names queue 0 slot 0 of turn 0

The gso packet id is ( turn * slots + slot ) * queues + queue, so the first packet of the first turn on queue 0 has id 0. Nothing treats 0 as no packet today (finish and abort check the pointer against the slot), but a caller that keeps 0 as its own empty value would lose that packet. Decide whether the id should start at 1.

From: Piece K, cold reader

### Portable server transport on the shared buffer handoff

PR #1043 (refactor/v1.1.x/server-shared-handoff, extraction E5) moved the portable and gso server transports off their hand-written bank queues onto rocketnet_buffer_handoff_t (sdk/rocketnet_buffer_handoff.h). Its gso half is overtaken by the rebuilt gso transport (#1103), which rewrites sdk/rocketnet_server_gso_linux.cpp and also changes sdk/rocketnet_driver_builtin.cpp. After the rebuilt gso lands, redo the portable half alone on main (the portable TX and RX commits and the rocketnet_buffer_handoff_started helper), with its gates: rnportabletx, rnportablerx and rnbufferhandoff TLC, the unit mutation cases and the light memory pins. With it, give the portable receive worker what the rebuilt transports have: it runs no prefilter (sdk/rocketnet_driver_builtin.cpp about 613-645, drop hooks NULL about 1962-1966), so junk reaches the main thread (bounded per update), and datagrams held in its banks at stop are counted nowhere (about 932-944), so RECEIVE_DROPPED_STOPPED reads 0 on portable. Not worse than v1.0.0.

From: Open-PR triage 2026-11-13: #1043 not landed; review before v1.2.0, finding PO1

### ASan red zones between the rio registered region's arrays

In an AddressSanitizer build the rio transport's sized block (rocketnet_rio_sized_layout: slot bytes, retry slices, process arrays, drops, each bank's data, from and packet bytes) carries poisoned red zones between its carves. The registered region laid out by sdk/rocketnet_rio_layout.h (send frames, send addresses, receive slices, receive addresses; one RIORegisterBuffer) does not: its offsets are the layout RNRioLaneLayout models and the trace check binds, so a pad there changes a modelled layout. Add the pads to the layout and its model together, or record why that region stays uncovered.

From: #1047 merge with the rebuilt rio

### ASan red zones between the rebuilt io_uring transport's carved arrays

#1047 carved red zones into the replaced io_uring transport's bank block (rocketnet_server_uring_buffers_create). The rebuilt transport (#1104) removed that block; its carved allocations are now in sdk/rocketnet_uring_queue_send.cpp, sdk/rocketnet_uring_receive_queue.cpp and sdk/rocketnet_uring_send_queue.cpp, each one rocketnet_malloc of a layout. Add ROCKETNET_RED_ZONE_CARVE to each where the layout is not a modelled or kernel-registered region, and record why where it is.

From: #1047 merge with the rebuilt io_uring

### The io_uring provided buffers are 264 MiB a queue whatever the GRO tier

With ROCKETNET_SERVER_TRANSPORT=io_uring forced over the whole functional suite, test_lifecycle_transport peaks at 1269 MB resident against 698 MB, which is the suite's per-case bound (suite_case_rss_mb), not a plan bound. The cause is the receive buffers: 4096 buffers of 66 KiB a queue (ROCKETNET_URING_RECV_BUFFERS, ROCKETNET_URING_RECV_BUFFER_BYTES), 264 MiB a queue and four queues by default, made resident once the multishot writes into them, whether or not UDP_GRO was granted. Size the buffers by the tier (a buffer need only hold a whole datagram without GRO) or lower the count, and say so in the plan.

From: Piece L (io_uring), amd-3 run and cold reader

### A cancel answered -EALREADY in the io_uring worker

The worker counts a cancel it submitted when its completion arrives (rocketnet_uring_queue_worker_reap_one, ROCKETNET_URING_TAG_CANCEL). A cancel the kernel answers -EALREADY (the target already completed) reads the same as one that took effect; the model (RNUringQueueWorker.tla CancelRecv, CancelWake, CancelPoll) has one outcome. Check the worker against the answers and add the case to the model.

From: Piece L (io_uring), cold reader

### Offline cpu holes in the io_uring pin

rocketnet_uring_pin_check refuses a cpu at or past the online count, but a machine with cpus offline has holes below that count (cpu 5 offline, cpu 6 online). A pin to a hole is refused by the kernel, counted, and the worker is confined to its own mask past the OS's cpus (rocketnet_uring_pin_confine_words, which never names a hole), so it is placed but not where the config said. Read the online mask (sched_getaffinity or /sys/devices/system/cpu/online) and place the workers on online cpus past the OS's.

From: Piece L (io_uring), cold reader

### A transport thread runs on its creator's mask until its first call

Every transport thread (io_uring and gso queue workers, the XDP thread, and the other transports' network threads) pins itself as its first call, so between rocketnet_platform_thread_create and that call it runs on the creating thread's mask, which may hold cpu 0 (the OS's on Linux); the gso creator also raises the priority in that window. Give rocketnet_platform_thread_create an optional affinity (pthread_attr_setaffinity_np on Linux) so the thread starts on its placement: one place in the platform layer, used by every transport. Also: _SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN is a count, used as the highest cpu id, so a machine with an offline cpu in the middle is misjudged (read the online set instead).

From: Piece K cold reader; piece L (io_uring) second cold reader

### io_uring receive refusals that are not in the server's drop reasons

The rebuilt io_uring transport's receive drop totals are the worker prefilter's and the bank's reasons plus refused completions (RECEIVE_FAILED). A truncated source (URING_RECEIVE_DROPPED_SOURCE), a completion naming no buffer (URING_RECEIVE_DROPPED_NO_BUFFER) and segments past one receive (URING_RECEIVE_DROPPED_OVERFLOW) are counted only in their URING_ rows, where the replaced transport also folded them into RECEIVE_FAILED and BANK_FULL. A source drop is also counted once per completion, even for a GRO batch of several datagrams (sdk/rocketnet_uring_receive_queue.cpp about 598-624), where gso counts each datagram into RECEIVE_FAILED (sdk/rocketnet_server_gso_linux.cpp about 1052, 1197-1205). Decide the fold and the unit, and test both by value.

From: Piece L (io_uring), second cold reader; review before v1.2.0, finding L2 (2026-11-13)

### RNUringQueueReceive: Complete without F_MORE

The model's Complete takes a datagram completion and keeps the multishot armed; the code (rocketnet_uring_receive_queue_cqe) also ends it when the completion has no IORING_CQE_F_MORE and arms again on the next pass. Add the ending to Complete with a reversed witness, and a trace point.

From: Piece L (io_uring), cold reader

### A malformed UDP_GRO control message is passed as one datagram

A receive whose control area is truncated or malformed (GRO_CMSG_FAULTS) is taken as one datagram, so a coalesced buffer of several datagrams reaches the prefilter as one long one and fails its checks there. Decide whether the receive module should drop it by name instead, with a counter row, and test the split on a malformed control area.

From: Piece L (io_uring), cold reader

### The io_uring receive re-arm spins on a kernel that refuses multishot

A kernel that refuses multishot receive (Linux before 6.0) ends every arm at once; the worker arms again on its next pass without a bound, burning its core. The refusals are visible as RECEIVE_FAILED now (the receive module's ERRORS reach the drop totals). Bound the re-arms, back off, and name the kernel in the create log.

From: Piece L (io_uring), cold reader

The two-machine load_split delivery proof with an xdp server and portable clients failed 1 of 5 runs on v1.0.1 (one client RELIABLE_TIMED_OUT) and 1 of 4 on v1.0.0 (missed due slots), so it predates v1.0.1. Find each cause on quiet hosts.

Since v1.0.1, io_uring picks the send socket per send run instead of per batch, so consecutive packets to one client can leave on different reuseport sockets within one update. Measure any extra reordering against v1.0.0.

## Existing nightly proof debt

Incomplete proof measurements remain explicit failures under the existing nightly workflows. These are distinct from the completed audit correspondence repairs.

### Eleven recorded TLC benchmark timeouts

The committed RUNS.tsv records FAIL/124 at the 110-second limit for the eleven declared timeout-debt cases in CASES.tsv: ClientConnection LArbitrary, LCrash, SNone, SAlternate, SBurst and SArbitrary; ReplayWindowMid; RNEndpointTwoWay and RNEndpointPartial; RNClientIoDecrypt; and SessionAcksLive. The TLC records workflow checks each only to that bounded record; the weekly tlc-debt.yml runs each to its declared result as its own job, two at a time, and keeps its evidence. Failure, cancellation or resource exhaustion is not a proof. Fresh measured records require a reviewed commit; the workflow does not commit them automatically.

From: proofs/tla/CASES.tsv and RUNS.tsv; existing TLC nightly; #833

### ACK run leaf has no symbolic proof; bound 8 is checked exhaustively

ESBMC 8.5 cannot encode rocketnet_ack_apply_run at any run bound: each write through a pointer with a symbolic offset into the 260 KB endpoint (the visit's record->acked) becomes a byte-level update of the whole object, and bound 1 already stops Out of memory at 150 GB (proofs/cbmc/INVENTORY.md, ACK run measurements). Z3 answered unknown every night 11-01..11-12. Since 2026-11-12 the Nightly ACK proof runs ack-run-exhaustive-8 instead: every ring position, run length 1..8, ack pattern and highest offset, in three sequence blocks, with a negative control, a vacuity plant and four planted bugs that must each fail. That is exhaustive native testing, not a proof; blocks between 1 and the last rest on a translation argument, and lengths 9..4096 are not covered. A symbolic proof needs a verifier that keeps &a[i] as an index (CBMC does, but cannot parse the C++17 leaf) or an index-form write in the visit, which is an SDK change.

From: proofs/cbmc/INVENTORY.md; .github/workflows/nightly-ack-proof.yml; #797

### Model the nested calls and the refused look's three writes in RNFillPhase

proofs/tla/RNFillPhase.tla leaves out the nesting depths, and takes a refused look (sdk/rocketnet_fill_phase.cpp rocketnet_fill_phase_fill_begin: the word, the owner and the word again) as one step. A cold reader found an interleaving in that gap: a call that a main thread call ran inside puts the owner back while the word still reads as held at depth 1, the thread it gives the client back to reads its own next call as nested, and its end leaves a fills_in line it never entered, after which every main thread call is refused. Fixed by the order of the writes (the word goes back to the lock's form first); no test fails without the fix and no model step sees it. Add the nested path and the three writes to the model with a reversed witness for the old order, and a trace point between the writes.

From: Piece G (sending from the game threads), cold reader finding 1

### Model the chunked payload ring claims at the layout level

rocketnet_server_payload_ring_take (sdk/rocketnet_server_transport.cpp) claims payload ring slots in chunks held on per-thread lines, with index arithmetic on a packed [end:32][next:32] word, a guard, a clip at send_capacity and a give-up when another thread on the line installs first. proofs/tla/RNServerPayloadRingLayout.tla still models one fetch-add a slot. Model the same arithmetic at capacity 3 or 4 with reversed witnesses: a lost install that keeps its first slot (one client's packets then leave out of start order; test_server_fill_ring_chunk_lost_install_keeps_start_order pins the fix), and a line's unused slots not marked empty before the flush.

From: Piece G, cold reader finding 2; the layout rule

### RNSendReserve: TailsNamed is implied by NeverStarved

As defined, with no other thread holding a tail RoomFor and RoomPastTails are the same predicate, so unnamed implies starved: the invariant TailsNamed adds nothing NeverStarved does not check, and its witness MCRNSendReserveBrokenNoTailReturn.cfg would fail NeverStarved too. The model also marks the counter choice at the decision, where the code reads the tails after the take back and the retest. Restate TailsNamed so it can fail alone, and move the choice to where the code makes it.

From: Piece G, cold reader (TLA+ section)

### RNSendReserveCalls: a Capacity per send queue

send_capacity_available is one number: with several send queues it is the fewest free slots of any queue, an upper bound on what the next start may find. The send reserve's per-queue room (send_queues, send_queue_of, send_room_queue) is read by the reserve, but RNSendReserveCalls models one Capacity. Model a Capacity per queue, bind the code's call to it in the trace check, and say in the transport standard what a start on a queue with room may rely on. The trace check is narrower than that today: tests/tla_trace_send_reserve.cpp (213-221) only ever runs one queue, so the per-queue reserve code in sdk/rocketnet_server_transport.cpp (about 1060-1093, 1207-1253) is on no checked trace and a defect there cannot turn it red. Walk several queues.

From: Piece M follow-on, cold reader; review before v1.2.0, finding M3 (2026-11-13)

## Found while preparing v1.0.1

Defects, gaps and measurements found by the v1.0.1 review and test campaign that a point release does not carry. Each is checked at the cited code first.

### io_uring setup ENOMEM: a status, or the gso fallback

Under kernel memory pressure io_uring ring setup can fail with ENOMEM, and create treats it as an ordinary refusal: auto falls to gso and a pinned io_uring ends NO_TRANSPORT_FOUND. Reporting an out-of-memory status instead would stop that fallback, a behaviour change, so it belongs in a minor release. Decide which, then pin it with a test.

From: v1.0.1 CI: io_uring ENOMEM on a loaded bench, errno now logged by posix_check

### xdp stop: count the handoff buffers it abandons

When xdp stop gives up on a transmit ring that has stopped draining, the handoff buffers it abandons are counted in no counter. Count them, so a stop that dropped packets says so.

From: v1.0.1 xdp worker fixes (stop bound for a stalled TX ring)

### Linux UDP sends: count interface queue drops per socket

On Linux a datagram a full interface queue drops is reported to the send call only with IP_RECVERR set; without it the kernel counts the drop per host (Udp SndbufErrors) and SEND_FAILED never sees it (docs/LINUX.md section 7). Set IP_RECVERR on the portable, gso and io_uring sockets, so the send call returns ENOBUFS and the drop counts in SEND_FAILED, and drain the socket's error queue (MSG_ERRQUEUE). Cost: with IP_RECVERR every ICMP error for a destination (port or host unreachable) is queued on the socket and reported by its next receive call, so each receive path needs an error-queue drain (one more call per drain while the queue is not empty) and a classification of what it reads, where today those errors never reach the socket (section 7).

From: read-everything review: SEND_FAILED's claim about a full interface queue

### xdp: EBUSY with the carrier off is counted per frame

With the link carrier off, each frame's transmit wakeup EBUSY counts in SEND_FAILED on its own, so a down link inflates the counter by its send rate. Decide whether such a run counts once, as a hard wakeup error does.

From: v1.0.1 xdp worker fixes

### Measure xdp worker lock contention

Try-lock failures between the main thread and the xdp workers were never measured. Measure them on a two-queue guest on a quiet bench before any change.

From: v1.0.1 xdp review, item M6

### xdp receive path reads the platform clock

The xdp receive path still reads rocketnet_platform_time() instead of the update's time. Passing the time in needs the driver seam widened.

From: v1.0.1 xdp gateway review, item L13

### xdp TX queue choice is an unkeyed hash; gso send bank at 32768 clients

xdp picks the TX queue with an unkeyed FNV-1a of the destination (rocketnet_server_socket_send_queue), so spoofed sources can aim replies at one queue: key it per server. gso's fixed 4096-packet send bank is short at max_clients 32768.

From: v1.0.1 review

### io_uring receive view larger than the payload batch

Below 640 clients the io_uring receive view is larger than the server payload batch. Check what the server does with the difference and pin it.

From: v1.0.1 server transport review, item F5

### Functional case: large messages under loss

The functional suite sends reliable messages above 8 KiB only without loss (1 MiB lossless). Add a lossy case with large blocks in the existing harness.

From: v1.0.1 guarantees review

The DST end check excuses the last 20 sequences and every ended session and caps messages at 16 KiB; the chunk resend cap is pinned by one assertion; the receipt outcome of sends in flight when a connection ends, and fresh serials after a reconnect, are not checked. Strengthen each.

From: v1.0.1 guarantees review

### Models that no longer match their code

RNClientIo and its three rings, the MCRNSecurityTables switches, and the expire_floor layout in the token tables no longer match the code. Bring each model back to its code.

From: v1.0.1 review

Model citations point at source line numbers (for example ServerSession.tla citing rocketnet_server_transport_disconnect_client by line), and check_tla_coverage.py enforces them, so a function moving 21 lines forced every serversession case to be rerun. Cite by function or action name so a move does not stale the records.

From: Owner request, 2026-11-10

### Transports repeat themselves: share socket setup

The transports are large and repeat each other: socket setup is duplicated between gso and io_uring and between iocp and rio. Share it.

From: Owner request, 2026-11-10

### Windows transport gaps

The IOCP create-failure poll is unbounded (RIO's is bounded). The IOCP unit tests exercise queue_pop while production uses queue_pop_before. The USO fallback is untested.

### Functional cases that assert exact delivery over real sockets

Windows functional cases and the gso and io_uring functional cases assert exact delivery over real sockets, so a host dropping a datagram under load turns them red. Assert what the library promises instead.

From: v1.0.1 review

### Transport fault counters with no public reader

transport_faults feeds no production counter, and the client IOCP, gso and I/O fault counters have no public reader.

From: v1.0.1 review

### Client disconnect and the address-family race

rocketnet_client_transport_disconnect does not commit the family race (update does since v1.0.0), so after a disconnect before any cookie the I/O thread polls until stop. A send_batch_progress result out of range retries forever.

The staged fakes in test_unit_public_link_simulator.cpp (staged_fake_t), test_unit_driver_loopback.cpp (wt_staged) and test_transport_control.cpp still claim at finish, unlike the transports they stand for.

From: v1.0.1 review

sdk/rocketnet_test_vectors.h says its data mirrors the standard's appendix byte for byte, but most of its arrays are not printed there; the update-time clamp comments in the client and server transports say a bad time is 'loud in a debug build', which a reviewer found stale. CMake builds the test_platform_primitives binary, but no workflow runs it. Run it in CI.

Every row of tools/nightly_dispositions.txt names a pull request that is now merged or closed, so the nightly watch reports each as STALE; and the nightly workflows added since (fuzz, msan, toolchains, real-load, frame-budget and others) have no row at all, so the watch is red on them (seen by the release cutter on main 659e0b8d6, 2026-11-13). ### Reconcile: tell a refused-then-resent send from a real drop

The harden_load reconcile counts the kernel's SndbufErrors as named drops in the server-to-client chain. When the 1 MB socket send buffer is full the kernel refuses a gso send and the gso worker sends it again, so nothing is lost: on main 3218cf5f6 (X710 pair) library_sent equals library_received and players deliver 100%, yet every gso row reports chains=FAIL on 124k to 571k of them (REMEASURE-MAIN.md, gso). Count the refusals the transport resent in their own term, apart from sends the kernel refused and nothing sent again, so the chain still fails a real drop.

From: gso re-measure on main 3218cf5f6

## Trace check: gaps the README declares

What proofs/tla/README-TraceCheck.md says the trace check trusts rather than enforces (v2, 2026-11-12, after three cold reads). Each item says what enforcing it would take.

### Check the spec's own invariants on every trace

The trace cfg allows INVARIANT TraceConsistent only, so the spec's invariants are checked at the model's small sizes and never on the trace at the code's real sizes: code that follows a model which is wrong at 4096 slots passes. Enforcing it: an invariants list in each LAYERS row, the checker verifying each is a plain state predicate of the spec (the reach-predicate check already does this) and allowing INVARIANT lines for exactly those names, the writer emitting them, and a planted row whose model breaks an invariant only past its TLC size. Cost per layer: no extra TLC run, since the invariants are evaluated in the clean trace's existing run, once per record (401 at the default 400 steps). An invariant over a fixed array costs about slots x records evaluations, about 1.6 million for a 4096-slot ring at 400 steps, a few seconds on the bench and unmeasured until the first such layer lands. A plant trace stops at its rejection, and the plant run must not take the invariants, or a planted invariant break could stand in for the trace rejection the plant must cause.

From: Trace check v2, third cold reader (README 'What the check trusts')

### Refuse a copy of library code in a layer's test file

The walk must call the library, not a copy of it left in tests/tla_trace_<layer>.cpp beside a real sdk include. Today a reviewer checks this by reading the file. Enforcing it: after the clean build, run nm on the layer's object file and refuse any defined symbol with the library's prefix (rocketnet_) or any name the sdk files define. Also refuse a layer file that defines a function an sdk header declares. This needs the object path from CMake ($<TARGET_OBJECTS:tla_trace>, written next to tla_trace_config.txt) and nm or dumpbin on each OS. Add a planted row that copies one sdk function into the example.

From: Trace check v2, third cold reader

### Read the trace binaries' configuration from the layer's own unit

CONFIG is printed by tests/tla_trace.cpp, so a COMPILE_DEFINITIONS set on one layer's source file, or a configuration macro without the ROCKETNET_ prefix, changes the layer's code without the checker seeing it. Enforcing it: CMake refuses source-file COMPILE_DEFINITIONS on tests/tla_trace_*.cpp. Each layer's walk prints CONFIG through a macro in tla_trace_record.h expanded in its own unit. The macro list is every identifier an #if of the included sdk files tests, read from those files, not a fixed list of ROCKETNET_ names. Add planted rows for a per-source define and for an unprefixed macro.

From: Trace check v2, third cold reader

### Find why TLC sometimes prints no behaviour for a plant's violation

TLC 2.19 exits 12 on a plant trace and reports the invariant violated, then sometimes prints no behaviour; the statistics lines that follow are printed, so the log is not cut off. tools/tla_trace_check.py reruns such a plant up to five times and prints PLANT-ATTEMPTS (#1106). Ruled out on byte-identical inputs of the msgxsendruns seed 1 plant (hetzner1, 2026-11-13): TLC's -seed and -fp index (both pinned, -workers 1: a behaviour in 5/10, 6/10 and 7/10 runs for three pairs) and a shared or reused metadir (a fresh directory and -metadir each run). Start from a TLC-side cause: the trace file's write and read-back at the violation.

From: Piece P, #1093 trace shard 0/6

### Refuse a reach predicate that already holds in the first state

tools/tla_trace_check.py checks that each row's reach predicates are reached in some clean trace (a TLC run with ~predicate as the invariant). A predicate that holds in the initial state, or always, passes that check without proving any edge was walked. Refuse a predicate that holds at the first record, with a planted row.

## Found while landing and re-measuring the v1.1.x pieces

Known and not done after the transport work landed on main as v1.1.x point releases and was measured again from main (2026-11-13). Each says where it is and how it was found.

### io_uring at peak: whole segmented sends dropped at the server's device queue

On the X710 pair with 2 io_uring threads, peak load and no game load, the server's fq_codel queue drops whole UDP_SEGMENT sends: each is one player's 15-packet tick, so 2 to 13 drops in a 60 second row lose 30 to 195 packets (s2c 99.9997 to 100%; players whole, rows pass). The kernel accepted the sendmsg, so the transport counts the packets sent and nothing names the loss. The same rows also see 8.6 to 10.7 million EAGAIN completions a peak row against the documented 1,000,000-byte send buffer, where gso on the same pair and buffer sees 124k to 571k; a 4096-entry ring of sends in flight per queue is the likely reason, not measured. gso and XDP on the same pair: sent equals received. Tuning deferred by the owner ('we can do fine tuning later').

From: io_uring re-measure on main 3afea2aed, rows U1 and r2-r4 (REMEASURE-MAIN, io_uring)

### Reconcile: a dropped segmented send is 15 packets, not 1

The harden_load reconcile names the server's qdisc drops by the qdisc's count, which counts a dropped GSO skb once. At peak each skb carries 15 packets, so every such drop leaves 14 packets in the unnamed gap and the s2c chain fails on a loss it could name. Count the segments of a dropped skb (or read the qdisc's byte or packet drop totals), so the chain names the whole loss. Separate from reconcile-sndbuf-resends.

From: io_uring re-measure on main 3afea2aed: lost = 15 x qdisc dropped in every run

### URING_SEND_DEFERRED: the row text says something other than what is counted

sdk/rocketnet_counters.h says the row counts send calls that returned with sends not yet completed or staged slots not yet submitted. The code adds the worker's SOCKET_FULL to it (sdk/rocketnet_uring_counters.h), which sdk/rocketnet_uring_queue_worker.cpp counts once per send completion that came back -EAGAIN (send buffer full; the run is sent again after POLLOUT); in every re-measure row it equals the kernel's SndbufErrors exactly. Make the text say what is counted, or count what the text says.

From: io_uring re-measure on main 3afea2aed

### PREFILTER_WRONG_VALUE seen once on io_uring under heavy bench load

A Debug functional row of the io_uring piece reported PREFILTER_WRONG_VALUE 1274 once, under heavy load on amd-3; 12 reruns did not reproduce it and the cause was not found. A DEV-only sampler now records the first refused datagrams (source, length, first 16 bytes) in sdk/rocketnet_receive_prefilter.h and prints them in the clean-run report. When it recurs, read the samples; the open question is whether a datagram can reach the io_uring prefilter with wrong bytes or length (provided-buffer index, completion length, GRO split, a buffer returned while still referenced).

From: Piece L (io_uring), gate at ad93b2ad6

### Distribute the server update with task callbacks in the config, only on measured need

The split server update (update_receive, update_client, update_finish) landed as an opt-in; rocketnet runs no job system of its own. If a measured row shows the game's own job system cannot spread the update well enough through the public calls, add box3d-style task callbacks to the server config, off by default (see how box3d and fixed3d do it), and not before.

From: Owner rulings on piece I, 2026-11-13 (V12-ON-MAIN)

### Windows: RIO and IOCP reach their measured thread counts only with a specific bind address

RIO with more than one lane and IOCP with more than one completion worker refuse the wildcard bind, so a server bound to the wildcard runs one RIO lane or one IOCP completion worker. The peak row needs 6 RIO lanes and 2 IOCP completion workers with 2 send threads (AWS m7i.16xlarge rows, 2026-11-13). Either make the measured count the default when the server binds a specific address and say plainly that the wildcard runs one, or lift the wildcard refusal.

space-frame-row passes --transport xdp fixed, so the gso and io_uring re-measures called scripts/harden-pair with the same server arguments by hand. Take the transport (and its queue count) as an argument so every Linux transport's row is one command.

Update the performance document's rows from the re-measure on main (XDP 59890655d, gso 3218cf5f6, io_uring 3afea2aed, and RIO, IOCP and macOS as their rows on main come in), with the minimum network threads each transport needs for the peak row. Done by the document's author.

From: Re-measure on main, 2026-11-13

## Found by the review before v1.2.0, not fixed for it

Findings of the review that started on 2026-11-13 (main 5488a5443) that are not being fixed for v1.2.0. Read, not run, unless an entry says so; each names the file and lines.

### XDP: the gateway refresh blocks the main thread every 5 seconds

On XDP, rocketnet_server_socket_receive_packets (sdk/rocketnet_server_socket_linux.cpp about 4745) runs the gateway refresh on the main thread every 5 s (rocketnet_xdp_gateway_refresh, sdk/rocketnet_xdp_frame.h about 1473, through rocketnet_server_socket_resolve_gateway about 648). rocketnet_gateway_netlink_refresh opens a NETLINK_ROUTE socket, dumps the whole route table for the family (RTM_GETROUTE with NLM_F_DUMP), then queries the neighbour (RTM_GETNEIGH), each receive blocking with a 1 s timeout (sdk/rocketnet_gateway_netlink_linux.cpp about 751-840, 1006); with both families, twice. The cost grows with the host's route count and can block the main thread up to the timeout under rtnl contention; it does not show on a bench with a small table. Resolve it off the main thread (on a network thread), or query the one destination without blocking.

From: Review before v1.2.0, finding X5

### IOCP stop can hang on a receive reposted after its owner's worker exited

Any IOCP worker reposts a refused receive on the owning endpoint's socket (sdk/rocketnet_server_iocp_windows.cpp about 1684-1699), reading stopping (1184) before it raises pending and posts (1235-1237); each stopping worker cancels only its own endpoint's receives and exits when the global pending count reads 0 (1501-1516). A repost that lands after its owner's worker has exited is never cancelled: rocketnet_server_iocp_stopped never turns true, destroy refuses (3722-3726) and create's failure path waits with no bound (3027-3035). Very rare. The model hides it: RNIocpEndpoints.tla Retry (89-96) checks ~stopping and posts in one atomic step. Fix: raise pending before the stopping check, or have every stopping worker cancel every endpoint's receives; split Retry in the model with a reversed witness.

From: Review before v1.2.0, Windows reader, finding W1

### Send capacity is reported for frames the caller cannot take, so an overloaded frame walks every client

send_capacity_available counts own frames and every queue's budget (sdk/rocketnet_server_transport.cpp about 1510-1528), more than the next start can take, so under overload the serial walk visits every client and is refused for each (sdk/rocketnet_message_server.cpp about 2073-2080, 2195, 2225): main thread work grows with the client count on exactly the frames that are already over. Report what the caller can take.

From: Review before v1.2.0, send reserve reader, finding M1

### One full send queue makes the send capacity 0 for every client

Capacity is the fewest free slots of any queue (sdk/rocketnet_server_transport.cpp about 1549, through io_send_room 984-1000), so one full queue stops sends to every client, including clients on queues with room. io_send_room_total (1101-1119) already does this right for disconnect drains. Use the client's own queue's room (or the total) for its start. See also send-reserve-multi-queue-capacity.

From: Review before v1.2.0, send reserve reader, finding M2

### io_uring stop-time send retry bound counts every refusal and never resets on progress

The io_uring worker's stop-time bound counts each refused send and neither waits nor resets when a send makes progress (sdk/rocketnet_uring_queue_worker.cpp about 185-196, 275-278), so a slow drain at stop can give up early; gso resets on progress and waits (sdk/rocketnet_server_gso_linux.cpp about 722-733). Only reachable when stop runs with sends outstanding. Match gso.

From: Review before v1.2.0, gso and io_uring reader, finding L1

### io_uring drops a send refused with ENOBUFS or ENOMEM, where gso retries

sdk/rocketnet_uring_queue_send.cpp (about 423-438) treats ENOBUFS and ENOMEM on a send as FAILED: the packets are dropped and counted. gso sends them again (sdk/rocketnet_server_gso_linux.cpp about 2554). Make the two transports treat a transient refusal the same way.

From: Review before v1.2.0, gso and io_uring reader, finding L3

### The XDP send side has models and no trace layer; the receive-ring walk never runs the real worker loop

No trace layer binds the XDP send half to its models: the buffer exchange publish, claim and recycle (sdk/rocketnet_server_socket_linux.cpp about 158-210, RNBankFifoLayout.tla), the producer publish and turn bump in rocketnet_server_socket_send_packets (about 3268-3316, RNDriverSendStaging.tla Publish), the worker's claim, copy, recycle and send-frame free list (about 5008-5156, WorkerRetire), and the stop drain (rocketnet_server_socket_send_idle about 3051, rocketnet_xdp_send_stall_pass in sdk/rocketnet_server_socket.h about 108, RNXdpSendDrain.tla). Only unit cases cover them (tests/test_unit_xdp_send_staging.cpp, tests/test_xdp.cpp). The xdp-receive-ring trace (tests/tla_trace_xdp_receive_ring.cpp about 287-460) calls the pass helpers in an order the walk composes and never runs rocketnet_server_socket_xdp_thread_function (about 4825). Add send layers, and drive the receive walk through the real loop.

From: Review before v1.2.0, XDP reader, finding X1

### An XDP server on a VLAN takes frames from other VLANs when the NIC strips tags

sdk/xdp/server_xdp.c (about 483-516) and sdk/rocketnet_xdp_frame.h (about 383-405) take an untagged frame on a tagged server. With receive VLAN offload on (the i40e and ixgbe default) native XDP sees every stripped frame untagged, so a frame of any VLAN the NIC accepts, or of the native segment, addressed to the server's address and port is processed, and the reply goes out tagged with the server's VLAN: layer-2 isolation is bypassed for the game port and spoofed sources skip the router's filters. Smallest fix: refuse a VLAN server unless rx-vlan-offload is off, or read the stripped tag (bpf_xdp_metadata_rx_vlan_tag, Linux 6.8 and later).

From: Review before v1.2.0, XDP reader, finding X2

### XDP accepts sources the kernel stack drops as martian, and does not verify checksums on receive

sdk/xdp/server_xdp.c has no source check, and userspace refuses only IPv4-mapped IPv6 (sdk/rocketnet_xdp_frame.h about 675, sdk/rocketnet_address.h about 65): 0.0.0.0/8, 127/8, 224/4, 255.255.255.255, the server's own address, ::, ::1, ff00::/8 and source port 0 reach the main thread and get replies. IPv4 header and UDP checksums are not verified on receive (rocketnet_xdp_frame_parse_vlan about 420-537), and the kernel fast path does not check the version nibble (server_xdp.c about 552). The socket transports get all of this from the kernel. Refuse these in the kernel program and check the sums.

From: Review before v1.2.0, XDP reader, finding X3

### XDP: datagrams received and not handed to the main thread at stop are counted nowhere

The XDP operations table passes NULL for receive_drop_totals (sdk/rocketnet_driver_builtin.cpp about 2523), the only feed of RECEIVE_DROPPED_STOPPED, so at stop (sdk/rocketnet_server_socket_linux.cpp about 4887-5285) the staged, ready, unread-tail (about 4761) and receive-ring datagrams are dropped uncounted. Every other rebuilt transport counts them. Feed the row, with a test that reads it by value. Separate from xdp-stop-abandoned-buffers, which is the send side.

From: Review before v1.2.0, XDP reader, finding X4

### The rio-lane trace checks the harness's own slot table, not the transport's

tests/tla_trace_rio_lane.cpp calls the real hash, lane_of, packet_id and decode (about 126-140) but keeps every state field itself (slot, issued, staged, starts, strayed, misrouted; about 56-68, 129-211): it picks the slot with its own loop and decides misrouted itself. The transport's slot take and frame check, start_packet, finish_packet, abort_packet and lane staging in sdk/rocketnet_server_rio_windows.cpp (about 485-514, 1713-1744, 4162-4198) never run under the trace, so NoReissue, FinishOwn and OneLanePerDest cannot go red for a library defect. The hash is called with family 1 where the transport passes to->type (134, 240), and the comment at line 11 overstates what is bound. Drive lane start and finish on the no-socket fixture and read the library's state, or say plainly what the layer binds.

From: Review before v1.2.0, checks reader C1 and Windows reader W3

### The iocp-admit trace binds only the admit verdict

tests/tla_trace_iocp.cpp (about 169-194) calls rocketnet_server_iocp_test_receive_admit for the verdict, then pushes to its own bank and increments its own full, refused and counted. rocketnet_iocp_bank_datagram (sdk/rocketnet_server_iocp_windows.cpp about 1309-1325) and the drop counters never run, so EveryDropCounted and Accounted are checked against the harness's arithmetic: a BANK_FULL datagram dropped uncounted stays green. Drive the real bank and read the library's counters.

From: Review before v1.2.0, checks reader, finding C2

### The xdp-gateway-refresh trace cannot see the refresh moved

tests/tla_trace_xdp_gateway_refresh.cpp (about 192, 240-253, 326) decides when the refresh runs with the walk's own phase string; the real call site (sdk/rocketnet_server_socket_linux.cpp about 673) never runs, and the untraced ReceiveWithoutRefresh is justified by assumption (tools/tla_trace_check.py about 157). The deadline part is bound; the ordering part (the model's RefreshInFill witness) is not, so a refresh moved into the send path stays green. Drive the walk through the real call site.

From: Review before v1.2.0, checks reader, finding C3

### finish_message and abort_message from the starting thread are not checked against game threads

In sdk/rocketnet_api.cpp (about 3642-3689) and sdk/rocketnet_fill_phase.cpp (about 203-210) the hand-over runs its main thread check only when another thread owns the client. When the owner is the caller or nobody, rn_server_pending_slot scans every connection's plain open.pending while other threads write theirs. rocketnet.h says one thread at a time, and nothing refuses a call that breaks it. Refuse and count it, as the other thread rules are.

From: Review before v1.2.0, threading reader, finding R3

### check_counter_observed.py accepts tests that assert nothing about a counter's value

This gate enforces that a counter row lands only with a test that reads it by value, and it accepts empty assertions. tools/check_counter_observed.py (about 426-434) excludes only a clause ending == 0, so check( v[X] >= 0 ), check( v[X] == 0u ), check( !v[X] ) and check( v[X] == v[X] ) count as observed; it accepts T name = v[X]; when any check anywhere in the file reads an identifier of that name (about 465-475); and the return path matches a function of the same name in any file (about 510-513). Run on a scratch tree, it reported 5 of 5 counters observed with five empty assertions; its 26 self-test cases have none of these forms. On the real tree 238 of 301 rows are observed by a value check and 53 more only through the loose paths. Close the three paths, add the forms as self-test cases, and give the 53 rows real value checks.

From: Review before v1.2.0, checks reader, finding C4 (run)

### msgx may resend a batch whose first packets the kernel already sent

sdk/rocketnet_msgx_send_runs.h (about 32-41, 330-374) takes a sendmsg_x that returns -1 as none taken: the run is kept and sent again whole from the same cursor (the worker retries every 1 ms, sdk/rocketnet_server_msgx_apple.cpp about 794-799, 879-903). The repo's own measured note says xnu can deliver part of a batch and still return -1 with no count (sdk/rocketnet_platform.cpp about 505-512, 2692-2701), and the client and portable pump handle that; msgx does not. If an ENOBUFS at peak does this, the delivered prefix goes out two or more times into a full queue: duplicates the client's replay window drops, sent counters under the wire, SEND_FAILED over on the error path. The model (RNMsgxSendRuns.tla) has the same assumption in its fake kernel. Open until measured: one peak row on the 10 GbE pair (received against packets_sent with send_dropped 0) decides; a loopback probe of 2000 batches of 64 never saw a refusal.

From: Review before v1.2.0, macOS reader, finding P3

### A strict option: refuse to start when a Linux transport worker cannot be kept off CPU 0

When the pin and then the fallback confinement are both refused (XDP leave_core_zero in sdk/rocketnet_server_socket_linux.cpp about 4236-4256, io_uring confine_worker in sdk/rocketnet_server_uring_linux.cpp about 411-431, and gso's fallback), the worker carries on with the inherited mask, CPU 0 included, for good: a cpuset limited to CPU 0 does this. The count and the warning are being fixed for v1.2.0. Left: an option, off by default, that makes the server refuse to start instead when the host has more than one CPU (a one-CPU host must still run).

From: Review before v1.2.0, Stella's finding S3
